provider: Ahrefs Keywords Explorer (keywords-explorer-overview) and SERP Overview, country=au
verdict_rule: the same rule the tr-TR and ko-KR files use: admitted when the top keyword clears 1,000 a month, OR when three or more keywords clear the 100 floor and the top one clears 500. Families are judged on all their keywords merged.
why_this_market: On the numbers this is the best market in the ranking and it is only second in the materialisation order because Australia had to be downloaded. The first ranking scored it on 16 keywords and 50,000 volume; 60 keywords read on 2026-10-05 put it near 740,000, with the most open SERP measured anywhere in this exercise and the highest commercial value by a long way.
the_headline_is_commercial_not_informati: esim australia reads 18,000 a month at a CPC of THREE DOLLARS FIFTY. That is the single most valuable keyword measured anywhere in this project, and it is not alone: esim usa $2.00, esim new zealand $1.80, esim japan $1.70 at 5,400, esim bali $1.70 at 4,100, esim europe $1.20 at 7,300. For comparison the entire Turkish connectivity set tops out at $0.50 and most of it reads $0.00 to $0.10. en-AU is the only candidate where the connectivity intent itself, rather than the travel content around it, is the reason to enter the market.

things to do in port douglas
things to do in byron bay
things to do in airlie beach
things to do in newcastle nsw
things to do in alice springs

what_the_measurement_settles: The city family is both large and shallow-difficulty in a way no other candidate matched. Melbourne reads 28,000 at keyword difficulty ZERO and Sydney 19,000 at 2. Twenty-three cities carry volume and the tail runs to Alice Springs at 1,200 and Newcastle at 1,500, so this is not three capitals and a cliff.

The named-entity family is the largest of any candidate: Taronga Zoo 52,000 at difficulty ZERO, Luna Park Sydney 23,000 at ZERO, Queen Victoria Market 13,000 at ZERO, against Sydney Opera House 45,000 at 48 and Uluru 60,000 at 73. The difficulty split is the useful part: the icons are contested and the second tier is wide open, which is a publication-ordering fact rather than a reason to skip either.

Outdoor entities carry both volume and difficulty 0 on the second tier: Cradle Mountain 19,000 at ZERO, Kakadu 12,000 at ZERO, Wineglass Bay 6,500 at ZERO, Grampians 3,900 at ZERO, Larapinta Trail 5,900 at ZERO, Overland Track 3,600 at ZERO. Great Barrier Reef at 42,000 and difficulty 85 is the one to publish last, not first.

The neighbourhood list is the weakest family here and it is still real: Surry Hills restaurants 4,800, Bondi cafes 800, Newtown bars 600, Fitzroy cafes 500, St Kilda cafes 200. Note this is the OPPOSITE split from Turkish, where the neighbourhood RESTAURANT list was dead at 20 and the cafe list was alive. In Australian English the restaurant variant is the strongest of them.

No family measured at or near zero. That is unusual and it is stated plainly rather than treated as confirmation: the 60 keywords were chosen to cover the families this inventory already builds, so a clean sweep means those families fit this market, not that every possible family would.

serp_evidence.verdict: THE MOST OPEN SERP MEASURED IN THIS EXERCISE

activities.city-things-to-do.reading: getawaycairns.com.au at DOMAIN RATING FOUR holds position 3 with 1,118 traffic and ONE backlink. cairnsurbanwalkingtours.com.au, also DOMAIN RATING FOUR, holds position 5 with zero backlinks. Tripadvisor DR 87 sits between them at 4, redballoon DR 68 at 6 and booking.com DR 93 only at 7. The AI Overview above cites travelmermaid, littlegreybox and shortgirlontour, which are independent travel blogs, not official boards or OTAs. Two DOMAIN RATING 4 sites in the top five is as open as a SERP gets, and it is the exact opposite of what the Korean and Indonesian equivalents showed.

outdoors.peak.reading: A question block at 1 and an AI Overview at 2 citing parks.tas.gov.au, discovertasmania, Wikipedia, australia.com and Tripadvisor. Then the organic head: ausweekendescapes.com.au at DOMAIN RATING 31 in position 3 with 2,081 traffic and ZERO backlinks, ABOVE Tripadvisor DR 87 at 4 and Lonely Planet DR 89 at 5. A zero-backlink independent page outranking both of those is the same answer the city family gave: in Australia the content wins and the authority does not. Two families sampled, two open readings.

connectivity.esim-country.and_this_is_a_different_SURFACE_not_a_di: This keyword does NOT belong to the Atlas inventory. The 1M candidate set is travel-content pages; esim australia is a product page, a different surface with a different template and a different owner. Its SERP is read here because the $3.50 CPC is the commercial case for entering en-AU at all, not because any row in this manifest would target it. Confusing the two would be the mistake: a travel page built to rank for a product keyword is a doorway page, and that is on the forbidden list.
connectivity.esim-country.reading: An AI Overview at 1 citing Telstra, Canstar, ALDI Mobile, Boost, Sim Local and Saily. Organic: Telstra DR 84 at 2 with 26,944 traffic, Telsim DR 55 at 3, ALDI Mobile DR 48 at 4 on FIVE backlinks with 5,406 traffic, Holafly DR 78 at 6 with 305 backlinks, Canstar DR 77 at 7 on FOUR backlinks, esim.com.au DR 29 at 8 with 1,726 traffic. Carriers, comparison sites and eSIM resellers. Holafly at 6 is a direct competitor to this product, and a DR 29 reseller holds 8, so the SERP is contested rather than closed: the incumbents are the same kind of business rather than unassailable publishers. That is the normal shape of a commercial SERP and it is a reason to enter the market, with the caveat that winning it is a product and link problem rather than a content-volume one.

serp_evidence.what_is_not_sampled: Three of five, and the three that matter are read: the city family (open, two DOMAIN RATING 4 sites in the top five), the outdoor-entity family (open, a DOMAIN RATING 31 page with zero backlinks above Tripadvisor and Lonely Planet) and the commercial keyword that makes the business case (contested by carriers and resellers). The POI and places families are unsampled in Australia and inherit the global shape classes.

duplication_risk_measured_not_assumed: en-AU shares /en/ with en-US and en-GB and adds pages rather than duplicating them. The measured basis: every URL in the manifest belongs to exactly one market, and distinct URLs per language equals rows per language exactly, en-GB 34,980 plus en-US 49,299 being exactly the 84,279 distinct /en/ URLs. The entities en-AU brings - Cairns, Noosa, Byron Bay, Launceston, Uluru, Cradle Mountain, Taronga Zoo - are ones neither existing English market reaches, because until now Australia had no home market and its entities were reachable only through the destination axis.
implementation_cost: LOW. No new language, so no alternate-name pass, no new sitelink language, no new local phrasing and no new mark fetch. One line in MARKETS, Sydney in ORIGIN, this file in the keyword overlay, and the capture that is already in flight.
